title: Rshan Hluf
text:
Hello! My name is Rshan Hluf. Welcome to my personal website. 


I am a Master of Data Science student at the University of British Columbia and a Mastercard Foundation Scholar, deeply interested in using data and AI to address the root causes of real-world community challenges. In addition to academics, I enjoy exploring new places, spending time in nature, and connecting with people from different backgrounds.
I value community engagement and enjoy participating in activities that allow me to meet new people, learn from different perspectives, and contribute to meaningful causes.
I try to maintain a balance between my studies, personal growth, and the things I enjoy outside the classroom. Since moving to Vancouver, I have enjoyed discovering the city and its beautiful outdoor spaces.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
My first weeks at UBC began before the MDS program officially started. We arrived early to become familiar with the campus and our new surroundings. This gave me some time to settle in and prepare for the journey ahead.
One of the highlights of this period was attending the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program orientation. It was an exciting opportunity to meet new people, connect with other scholars, and learn more about the community and opportunities available to us.
As the MDS program began on August 31, I was excited to meet my new classmates and learn more about the program. Starting a new academic journey came with both excitement and challenges, but these first experiences helped me feel more connected to UBC and prepared for the intensive months ahead.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Exploring Vancouver



Visiting Spanish Banks Beach


Outside the classroom, one of the highlights of my first weeks was visiting Spanish Banks Beach. Spending time there gave me an opportunity to explore Vancouver, enjoy the beautiful surroundings, and take a break from studying.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Finding Balance and Looking Forward
The first weeks have also taught me that graduate school is not only about studying. The MDS program moves quickly, so I am learning how important it is to balance education with life outside the classroom. Making time to rest, explore, and connect with others helps me return to my studies with more energy.
I am excited to continue developing my data science skills, learning from the people around me, and enjoying the experiences that come with living and studying in Vancouver. While I know there might be challenging moments, I am looking forward to the rest of the MDS journey!

title: About
text:
I have a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science and Engineeringfrom Mekelle Institute of Technology, Ethiopia. Through my studies and previous experiences, I developed a strong foundation in data analytics, AI/ML model development, and programming using Python, R, and SQL.
I am deeply passionate about transforming complex data into actionable insights and developing data-driven solutions that support better decision-making and build stronger communities.
Beyond my technical work, I have volunteer experience in national and international community development. I am also passionate about sustainability, women’s empowerment, and creating opportunities for underserved communities.
As the Founder of the Data for Change initiative and a Sustainability Ambassador at the University of British Columbia, I am committed to connecting data-driven innovation with social and environmental impact.
I strongly believe that data and AI are most powerful when they are used to empower people and create positive change.
My goal is to continue bridging data insights and social impact by modeling data-driven solutions that contribute to a more inclusive, sustainable, and equitable future.

Why Data Science
I am interested in using data science to understand real-world problems and support better decision-making. I joined the MDS program to strengthen my skills in data analysis, machine learning, and data-driven problem solving.

title: About

Outside of Data Science
Outside of my studies, I enjoy exploring new places, spending time with friends, and learning about different communities and cultures. Since arriving in Vancouver, I have also enjoyed discovering the city and balancing graduate school with life outside the classroom.
